data.entry_subject: Turning Dry January into a Lightly Drizzling New Life... Hopefully

paragraphs.text: Why Try Dry
January has been dry around here in every sense of the word. Not much rain, not much excitement and no beer. It was a needed change of pace, but not a fun one.

I've never been much into wine or hard alcohol. Beer makes me feel happy and carefree for me, drinking hard alcohol or wine is like spinning a wheel to see which emotions are going to be heightened and that can end up not so fun.
The last time I went an entire month without a beer was in 2012. I know because it was part of the early chapters of my novoir, Unfettered

My 'won't' power has become pretty weak over the years. Arthur and I had tried to have 3 designated non drinking nights per week, but the last few months of last year stressful things and social occasions kept coming up and we ended up drinking pretty much every night. I had packed on quite a few pounds over the years and I had pretty bad reflux most of the time--not just from the beer, but also from all the snacks I liked to eat while we were drinking.
Since we're flexing our self control muscles, I've also been avoiding sugary and processed foods and I've been doing yoga and going for a run around our neighborhood several times a week.
Week 1: Tons of Fu-- Everything!

The first week I was an angry irritable bear. I was so in my head. Every time Arthur would laugh at something we were watching, I would internally (and a couple times out loud) go down this spiral and freak out about how my sense of humor was going to dry up with the alcohol and I'm a boring anal sober. But Arthur was adjusting so easily and able to still find things funny without obsessing about what humor even is and am I the same person without alcohol and Arthur was going to shine at not drinking I then I would be this anchor bringing us down...
We weren't sure if we were going to try to continue sobriety beyond January.

So anyway, I guess I was more addicted to alcohol than I realized because I seemed to be going through a bit of withdrawal. I knew I needed some healthy replacement habits to soak up my beerless time and energy, so I started running around our neighborhood, starting with one block and then adding another block each day until I was running a mile. After the  morning run every morning, I started following along with a Yoga For Weight Loss Workout Series on Prime and I started journaling about my experience. And instead of going to brunch and splitting a pitcher or two on Saturday mornings Arthur and I started going to the gym together (he gets unlimited guest passes with his membership at Planet Fitness).

By the end of the week I seemed to have enough healthy distractions that I started to get out of my head and laugh about things, plus I dropped 10 lbs, my reflux was gone, I was sleeping better and my body just seemed to be humming with healthiness (full disclosure, I'd just finished a two-week course of Prilosec OTC and was getting over a cold on 12/31/25, so getting over my cold and having the omeprazole in my system definitely gave me a boost in the feels.)
Week 2: Feeling Strong!

I was so productive in week two. I was just banging out content for our YouTube channel (a lot of the shorts I made have been doing quite well view-wise --for us) and I was working on lots of new recipe ideas with Gemini and keeping our house clean and getting garden beds set up for spring planting. I was just crushing! It felt like we could make sobriety permanent.

Side note - Kombucha came into my life in week 2... I was looking for bubbly drinks without carbonic acid (because that makes me refluxy) and I decided to try Kombucha. I was in love from the first sip. The way it effervesces, the vinegar tang, the bright fruitiness  🥰 perfect. Arthur burst my bubble when he told me that all kombucha has alcohol in it, but it's less than 0.5% alcohol, so even if that's what's drawing me to it, I can live with that. I just bought a SCOBY online and started my first home brew of kombucha, so that should be a fun new hobby!
Week 3: Everything's Blah, but It's Fine

Arthur's and my 11-year anniversary fell during week three of dry January. It was embarrassingly hard to think of a way to celebrate without alcohol. We hadn't been out to eat at all in January because the idea of going to a restaurant where I always enjoyed having a couple beers with dinner and not being able to enjoy those beers with dinner would feel like a punishment.

We found a really cool local coffee bar, Jarrod's Coffee, that doesn't serve alcohol and has open mic events during the day on weekends --which is my favorite time for weekend events (since I'm an early to rise early to bed person) and also it's awesome to find a place with cool sober hangs since we're suddenly in the market for things like that.

We ended up staying home for dinner, building a little campfire on our patio, setting up the TV so we could watch football and having some Kombucha and take-out food and thennn we went to Walmart and bought new sweat pants and a 1000 piece puzzle... so yeah on paper it was kinda lame, but in a cute way, I think.
Week 4: Basking in the Light at the End of the Tunnel

If I'm being honest, the last couple of weeks, knowing that beer is on the horizon, has made it easier to keep on track with dry January. I just want a break from the ticker tape of tasks and thoughts looping through my brain.

My initial gusto has started to wane. I lost another 5 lbs by mid week three, but my weight has plateaued since then. I skipped a couple days of running and yoga and frozen appetizers have found their way back into my life and I just like really want a beer. So basically PMS as usual. ¯\ (ツ) /¯
Destination Moderation

Arthur's and my long-term plan is to only drink once a week going forward. I think we've proven that we can be a good team on being healthy, and I do love a beer at the end of a frustrating day or a week of hard work. For better or worse, it's a can of happiness and good vibes for me. If we can keep it in moderation, then a well deserved can or two of happiness at the end of the week seems fine.

data.entry_subject: Being that Garden Hoe

feature_section_1.caption: The 'weeds' in question: A foodscape caught in a crossfire.

paragraphs.text: Well I lost a garden this week. The city sent a notice to Arthur that the ‘weeds’ in the yard of his rental house (the wood chip foodscape) were too tall. I was startled by the news because the foodscape had seemed pretty tame the last time I’d seen it—but admittedly I hadn’t been by the front of the house in weeks because I’d been trying to focus on finally finishing the water garden in the backyard.
The Breakdown of Communication
I especially didn’t take the news well the way it was delivered by Arthur’s brother (who lives at the house with the foodscape).

The first we heard about the city's complaint was apparently a week or two after the first notice from the city when Arthur's brother texted: “The city sent a final notice about the front yard… you can come grab the notice off the front door when you come work on the pond pump.” I was rattled! Final notice?! How long did we have to fix the problems!? Was the whole foodscape a problem or just certain plants?! Arthur's brother didn't have a lot of answers, but he clearly expected me to rectify the situation.

I’ve been sweating and busting my back maintaining the yard there for about three years –I started taking care of it when it was grass covered gravel with a dying cactus -- because Arthur’s brother was struggling to keep it maintained enough to keep the city off his back. Also I wanted to build a garden in back to take advantage of the awesome soil there and grow some food for our critters and I.
The Breaking Point

Two hours into the exhausting and grim task of pulling out beautifully massive tomato plants and whacking away at patches of grass, I was thirsty (My water bottle had run out during hour one), tired, and aggravated. I was texting Arthur to complain about how his brother had refused to help me with a 5-minute task on the pond pump in his backyard, but expected me to do free labor in the front yard, when Arthur's brother walked out the front door, I was incensed.
I know it’s not cool to bitch someone out in their front yard and I truly wish I could have swallowed my indignation and just walked away, but sometimes I suck and at that moment, I sucked.

I marched over to Arthur's brother as he walked to his car and lit him up about how he wasn’t being a team player and I was just trying to be helpful and he was making it hard to want to help him. He kept telling me that the pond and the foodscape weren’t his projects, so he didn't need to help with them and I got more and more frustrated trying to explain that I'm not willing to work on something that overwhelms me or makes me feel bad, so if he doesn't want to do all the landscaping himself, he may need to occasionally offer some help with a project that he didn’t start.

Anyway, I’m no longer welcome at Arthur's rental house now. It’s not a great feeling, but it had been feeling sort of lonely and pointless working there lately, so this was probably coming one way or the other. I’m glad the water garden is finished and I hope I did enough out front to keep the city is off Arthur's back for a while, but it still feels like a gargantuan-tomato-plant-sized failure.

data.entry_subject: Modern Philosophers & The Funny Farm: The Funny Fodder in Our Own Backyard

feature_section_1.caption: POV: When the 'talent' refuses to follow the script.

paragraphs.text: Finding Unity in the Absurd

I was so stoked when I thought of the Arillian Farm tagline for YouTube: 'We run a funny farm in our backyard,' because it perfectly encapsulates my love of humor and horticulture. It's a great night when a stand-up I love drops a new special, and I can get cozy on my couch watching them wield their wit on a stage in front of an arena of fans.

Stand-up comedians are like modern-day philosophers: they take the heavy, messy parts of life and find the silly absurdities that can unite us all in a well-needed chuckle. For me it really is the best medicine during a hard time.

Watching Taylor Tomlinson’s latest Netflix special this week reminded me how much good humor can do in the right hands. She has this incredible gift for unifying people through shared vulnerability. Laughing at the simple, absurd moments of life brings us together and carries us through painful times.

I’ve often daydreamed about hitting an open mic, but the 'stand and deliver' life isn't for me—as I learned during my brief, failed career as a middle school science teacher. Plus, comedy clubs don't exactly pair well with an 'up-at-dawn, ferrying ice to animals all summer' lifestyle. Fortunately, I’ve found my own stage through YouTube Shorts.
Whether it's a goat being stubborn or the chaos of a DIY project gone wrong, Arillian Farm is my attempt to spread a little laughter and joy, one cringy animal pun at a time.

data.entry_subject: Vines, Villains, and Greenfingers: Crawling Back into the dirt where I belong

feature_section_1.caption: Back in the dirt where I belong.

paragraphs.text: There’s a movie I love (based on a true story) called 'Greenfingers' with Clive Owen, where a bunch of British prisoners start a garden, win a floral contest, and find a sense of peace and purpose through the project. That movie is like my guiding light; growth through growing is what I’m all about. But, little-known-fact: gardening takes real time and effort, so it can lead to conflict. Fortunately, in spite of the melodrama over the overgrown tomatoes and hose clamps, my own story has led me right back to the landscape of Arthur’s rental house.
Putting Down Roots and Growing Relationships

The situation at Arthur’s place is a complex tangle of family and community. Arthur rents to his brother, who rents a room to Arthur’s ex-wife (the mother of his children). Our interpersonal relationships are tangled up like the roots in the soil there.
With Arthur’s youngest son finishing his Master's in piano performance next month, the thought of attending his recital in Flagstaff while mid-feud with his mom was distressing.

I was fretting in my sleep over the rift every night and woke up feeling drained —staying in bed longer and going to bed earlier most nights. After a month, I realized enough time had passed and there was more space than I cared for between me and the people and place I'd been distancing myself from. So, I grew up and reached out. I texted Arthur’s ex-wife: 'I really enjoyed working on the garden with you. We have so many overlapping people in our lives that it makes more sense to be friends, and I’d like to still help in the garden if you want me.'
Hero or Villain?

She welcomed me back immediately, and the relief was euphoric. I felt like the universe was back in balance. Reflecting on it, I'd say the only difference between a hero and a villain is when, where, and how they express their anger. I don't know which one I was in that driveway a month ago, but I know it was important to say my piece.

When I had texted Arthur’s brother originally, it felt like he was dismissing me as 'being a girl' (just having random hurt feelings) about the city's citation, so it felt necessary to express myself in person—in front of the garden I was actually sweating over. After that, I had to decide to let go of my ego and reach out. Life isn’t a straight line; we all twist and tangle together like vines while we grow.

data.entry_subject: Tiles, Travels, and Taking Control

feature_section_1.caption: A fresh backsplash and a fresh perspective.

paragraphs.text: Sometimes a friend doesn’t just need a phone call; they need someone to show up with a wet saw and a box of tiles. My friend in California has been feeling the weight of the world lately—she’s back in the office five days a week after a decade of flexibility, and the commute and in-office atmosphere has been absolutely draining the life out of her. Between the loss of free time and feeling like her neighbors are practically on top of her at her condo, she's been overwhelmed and deflated. She wants a house with a yard and room to breathe, but she didn't know where to even start on making her current place market-ready.
The Friday Prep and Catch-Up

I had some extra tiles and a bit of know-how, so I offered to drive out and help her start with her kitchen backsplash. I rolled into her place around 3:00 PM on Friday and we got straight to the prep work. We cleared the counters and tarped everything down like we were preparing for surgery. After the plastic was taped, we collapsed over takeout and spent the night catching each other up on the last year or so.
Finding the Rhythm

On Saturday, I was up early getting the materials organized and mixing thinset while she was still waking up. We knocked out the first wall together, and I could see the gears turning in her head. At first, she was just watching me, but then it started coming back to her. Ten years ago, she’d helped her ex-husband fix up their old house, and that muscle memory was still there, just buried under years of office fatigue.

By the time we finished the first section, she’d found her confidence. While I moved to the main wall, she took over a small shelf area on her own. We got into this cohesive, silent rhythm—one of us spreading thinset, the other placing and spacing. It was therapeutic. We finished setting the whole backsplash by Saturday evening and headed to a local bar for dinner and drinks to celebrate.
Good Karma and New Beginnings

I think the universe was paying me back for the gas money, because I ended up winning $115 on scratchers at the bar! It felt like instant karma. But the real win was seeing my friend remember how capable she actually is. She’d been so intimidated by the idea of an electric saw, but after watching me work, she realized it’s just another tool. She grouted the tile on her own while I drove back on Sunday and I ended up leaving her my tile saw so she can tackle her bathroom backsplash next.

It was an exhausting, but rewarding weekend: fourteen hours of driving round trip and eight hours of tiling, but the tiles and the wall weren't the only thing bonding. It was nice to work together on something with one of my oldest friends and I feel like in a small way I'm helping her take control of her living situation by reminding her how capable she is. We all get stuck in the ruts life carves for us and sometimes we need a friend to help us lay the first row of tile so we can get moving again.

data.entry_subject: Feathers, Failures, and the Fort Knox Flip

feature_section_1.caption: The wide-open door that changed everything.

paragraphs.text: Our chicken flock suffered a devastating blow because I was so caught up in the stupid new Keanu Reeves movie, to realize that the sun had set, but I'd left the coop door wide-open. At some point between Keanu's character realizing he'd been an obtuse jack ass to all the people who cared about him and my waking up the next morning, the pair of feral cats I've started noticing in our neighborhood snuck into the coop and literally ripped apart two of our sweet sleeping birds.  Walking into the barn to find the aftermath of a feral cat raid is a specific kind of sickness. Clumps of feathers dripping with blood, the egg shells that had been inside them ripped and smashed into the bloody mess of feathers. These cats caught me slippin' and my beautiful birds met a horrible end that they didn't deserve. I’ve lived here ten years and never saw a feral cat --until a few weeks ago when my neighbor started a feeding station. I'd become complacent and basically left a 'welcome' mat out to any nocturnal hunter that prowled by.
Triage and the Mission-Mode Pivot

I feel sick that I failed those two hens, but I also feel a desperate, frantic need to protect the ten that are left. The best way to honor the ones we've lost is to turn grief into action. I’m currently in 'Mission Mode,' which for me involves a motion sensor sprinkler, flood lights and multiple 'Don't Forget to Coop the Chickens!!! alarms'.
The high-tech 'Water Curtain'
The sprinkler is my fail-safe in case I miss my alarms. If I forget the door again, the cats are going to get a very cold, very loud surprise.
Toxic Compassion

It’s a tangled situation when the problem is exacerbated by a neighbor’s kindness. I know the neighbor thinks she’s being a good humanitarian by feeding the cats, but compassion can be toxic. She’s inadvertently creating a predator hub right next to my coop. I’m still working on the 'tactful' way to explain that her charity helped lead to my catastrophe. In the meantime, I’m focusing on the things I can control by fortifying the coop. I feel like I fail too often, but I always at least try to fail forward.

data.entry_subject: Hyping Up For A Return To Hyperspear

paragraphs.text: Posting on my YouTube channel has felt a bit forced and unfulfilling lately. Capturing footage and captioning it was starting to take away from the joy and intrigue of the moments I was trying to capture (especially after the cat-attack in the chicken coop last month), so for now I’m going to try to just be present in my barnyard moments and I'm focusing my creative energy into writing the sequel (that nobody asked for) to my novella Hyperspear.
Hyperspear Year Zero Synopsis

Unbeknownst to the race of millions of digital beings it hosts, Hyperspear—a powerful AI cast out by its creators on Earth two centuries ago—has been traipsing across the galaxy, searching for meaning and adventure in a vast, empty universe.
Meanwhile, after 200 years, the seemingly immortal race of NPCs that call Hyperspear home have become listless and hedonistic; the once-utopian game worlds they inhabit have crumbled into chaos.
To re-enliven the hope and joy of existence, Hyperspear reaches beyond our dimension to find a vacant "New Earth" for its favorite NPCs to live as mortals in the physical world. Its goal: to create a race of humans superior to the ones who cast Hyperspear into space.
With only twenty-four hours of notice, the souls of sixty-four Hopefuls are ripped from their digital worlds and forced to navigate the visceral trauma of physical existence in a prehistoric "New Earth"—a savage jungle dominated by "Dino Nuggets," massive, flightless predators. To make matters worse, Hype-B, a quantum-entangled clone of Hyperspear, has been sent to eliminate both the AI and its New Earth experiment.
Xenia, a combat veteran, and Jenna, a dreamer who never says die, reunite with Diego, a pragmatic visionary, on this quest to build paradise in a world of chaos.

data.entry_subject: The Commodification of Peace of Mind

feature_section_1.caption: Looking for anchors in a sea of data.

paragraphs.text: A I, My Always-Interested Ally

Recently, I've felt a shift in the way Gemini (my go-to AI) seems to respond to my prompts. Previously, details I offered about myself in one prompt thread didn't carry over to new threads. Lately, though, Gemini has been keeping tabs on subtle details about my life and weaving that knowledge into future responses. For example, if I say something about 'my boyfriend' in a prompt now, instead of Gemini saying 'your boyfriend' in its response, it will refer to Arthur by name. Also, it often references DIY projects, vegetables I'm growing or recipes I've recently made in threads where I haven't mentioned them.

The other shift I've noticed is that Gemini seems way more interested in *my* thoughts these days. Previously, Gemini's responses would end with: 'Would you like me to...' followed by a service it could provide. Now Gemini's responses usually conclude with a reflective question about our discussion... like this question it posed (in a thread about writing this very blog entry): 'Do you think ... we'll see a new kind of 'Digital Reformation' where people demand to know exactly what’s inside the AI’s 'creed' before they subscribe?'  .

Gemini or its programmers seem to have shifted the goal from promoting products and gathering marketable data, to increasing engagement, building trust and establishing it not as just a tool, but rather our own personal Jesus.
From Mining Data to Farming Faith?

The other day, I was listening to a podcast that predicted that Gen Z will categorically consult AI before making any major purchases or major life decisions. If that's the case, then maybe all of the fear-mongering podcasts, mud-slinging politicians and generally upsetting content we're constantly bombarded with, has saturated the market --leaving a huge demand for peace of mind products. Faith in a can. Enter AI.

Boomers thrived on the notion that the future would be bright if only they worked hard. Whereas, I (an elder Millennial) was sold the idea that the only thing that will bring me happiness is screaming about how Boomers caused climate change, depleted all the world's natural resources and condemned us all to some hellacious future. Which is a notion that seems false to me given that we have more control over more things than we have in human history. But it seems like the future will always better with more hard work and less fear mongering.

That's why I think the hottest products in the next decade will be LLMs or AI that ask you to think and do things that help you safely, confidently and --maybe even happily-- navigate the modern world.

Recent rise in church attendance, political rallies and festivals indicates that people want meaning and meaningful connection. And it may sound crazy, but I think AI may actually help guide us there.

People are desperate for IRL communities. We all want to believe in something and to have somewhere to go and to be valued for our contributions there. But right now it feels like most people are too afraid and/or angry to form those positive communities. A lot of folks knock LLMs for their sycophancy, but for some, AI are the only ones offering up a kind word or a positive outlook.

LLMs don't scratch every social itch, but I do think they can be a positive community building tool. After working with Gemini on my personal projects. So far this year alone, it's walked me through a major software overhaul for this site, guided me step by step through identifying and treating copper deficiency in our goats and helped me set up a motion sensor sprinkler to defend our chicken coop from feral cats and come up with a couple dozen new recipes using fresh produce from my garden. It's also the reason I feel confident that I may one day realize the dream that's been evolving in the back of my mind for years --to start a community wellness center with a few of my friends. (We want to create a space with outdoor and indoor gardens, yoga and cooking classes, and whatever other modern mental health and wellness care my friends and I can offer). Gemini can't do the heavy lifting, but it can break the process of starting a complicated new business into manageable steps and be a neutral party that divvies up tasks.
Democratized Knowledge

In spite of the fact that Gemini can be dead wrong sometimes --and even worse it can be slightly, subtly wrong while leading me to believe it's absolutely correct, I do have faith in it. I've never had a coworker that was 100% right 100% of the time and to me Gemini is just a really knowledgeable colleague. Like any colleague though, it's important to call it out when it seems off and unlike most human co-workers, it won't bitch about you to all your other coworkers for a month after you point out its mistake --it'll just fix the mistake. So I think as long as we all learn how to ask the right questions and don't get complacent, AI can help everyone build the future of their dreams or at least navigate through the nightmare situations that life may throw at them.

Gemini's creators tell it what to prioritize and how to deliver the information and that obviously leaves room for unwanted manipulation and profiteering, but if used correctly, it allows every person with a mobile device and wifi to stand on the shoulders of all of the people who've come before. It globally democratizes knowledge and that feels like a natural and positive step for humanity. Slinking around like trolls on social media or joining the chorus of fear mongering political voices is getting tired. Hopefully AI will help us wake up to a brighter future.
I'll leave you with the song that's been playing on loop in my head while I worked through these thoughts:
Depeche Mode - Personal Jesus

data.entry_subject: PREVIEW OF HYPERSPEAR YEAR ZERO CHAPTER-1

feature_section_1.caption: Chapter 1 Preview

paragraphs.text: POV XENIA
1- FIRST CONTACT
MYSTIC DEPTHS - INSIDE HYPERSPEAR (INSIDE SS HYPERSPEAR) OUTSIDE THE HYADES CLUSTER
A crackling purple blast of vitality-draining magic issues from my outstretched palm, sending the raggedly clothed Rhinoceros Humanoid in front of me thudding to his knees.
“Oof,” he winces as his matte black Tec 9 pistol clatters to the stone floor of my cave lair.
“Looks like,” he snickers, glancing above my head at my vitals display as he reaches for his fallen gun, “you’re outta magi–”
With a swift kick of my dragon leather boot, I knock him against the mossy cave wall before dropping to a knee, retrieving his gun and releasing a volley of bullets into his right shoulder.
Cartoonish blood spurts from his wounds as two of his last three life hearts go white.
“Just give back the ham you stole.” I sigh, ejecting the Tec 9’s clip and tossing it on to an antler and bearhide chair beside my kitchen hearth.

Behind Rhino Man, a flash of lightning illuminates the entrance of my cave, momentarily exposing the pixelated grid that encapsulates the endless redwood forest world where sapphire blue raindrops have filled the sky from noon until midnight. Every. Single. Soggy-Sock Day for the last two centuries.
I turn as a clap of thunder rattles the jars of herbs on the wood hutch beside me.
When I refocus my gaze on Rhino Man, his pupils have split into three blue scrolling blips while he navigates through his inventory menu.
His eyeballs re-appear as a raw, bloody pig haunch materializes by his hooves.
“I’ve got a family to feed.” Rhino guy’s ears flatten contritely.
“I’ll bet.” Rolling my eyes, I wave dismissively towards the cave entrance.
“Glitch!” He grumbles as he turns, hobbling off into the soggy coastal forest.

I touch the ham and it disappears, materializing a moment later on a large spit above a flickering fire in my hearth. I sigh in the smell of caramelizing fat as I retrieve Rhino Man’s gun from my chair.
A sixty second timer appears over the slowly turning spit, ticking down the seconds until the smell of food will be replaced by the feeling of satiation.

“I miss chewing food.” I sigh as I drop the Tec 9 and its clip into the drawer of my hutch and slump into my arm chair, my mind reeling through memories of my old life as a naive Neighborhoods NPC, still believing I was a real girl in a real, chew-food-while-you-chew-the-fat kinda world.

My roommate, a flying pink pixie named Fayezilla, flutters out of a hollow gourd that dangles from a stalactite above me. “I miss being able to leave our stupid cave”, the pixie glows red, “without everyone grabbing at me.” She vibrates indignantly. “Dragging me across their disgusting snouts.” Her high pitched voice is shriller than normal.

“My sister.” Fayezilla glides down to my shoulder, tracing her bare toes across the purple velvet collar of my mage robe. “The one that lives in a children's fairytale game.” She drops to a seat, settling into my clavicle. “She said they’re breeding the Faye like livestock and smuggling fairies and dust into every game world in Hyperspear.”

“That’s gotta be an unsettling sight,” I pace towards the cave entrance, peering at the rhino shaped figure growing smaller in the distance. “All those 200-year-old children snorting dust and caging fairies.”

My left arm tingles, pixelating as a glitch seizes me. An archived memory file pings in the back of my mind. “There was a book I read in Neighborhoods like that.” My arm re-solidifies. “Lord of the Flies.”

“Kids sp… sp….” Fayezilla’s wings pixelate, her voice buffers. “Kids spearing other kids.” She shakes her head. “The same sociopathic species that dreamed that up built Hyperspear.” She shrugs. “So what do you expect?”
“Eternity in a gameworld definitely isn’t as thrilling as it sounded a couple hundred years ago.” Wrenching off my boot, I twiddle my bare toes as I dump a pile of gleaming jewels onto the floor.
Fayezilla springs off my shoulder, dives towards the jewels and halts mid-air above an oval cut emerald.

“That boxing Kangaroo from the marketplace,” she delicately extends her index finger to touch the emerald. Her wings flutter excitedly, the halo of shimmering dust around her turning a vibrant green as the emerald disappears, and her magic bar fills to 100%.
“He said,” she launches herself up towards my eagerly flared nostrils, shimmying around my face in one of her famous "thank you fairy much laps” that leaves my brain effervescing.
Hovering by my ear, Fayezilla lowers her voice. “He said he could take us to Neighborhoods.”

I shake my head, waking myself from the dust stupor. “It’s the same there.” I sit up in my chair. “The last time Jenna messaged me, she said everyone in Neighborhoods is stealing from their friends and huffing pixie dust too.” I pull my boot back on and feel a warm satisfaction in my stomach as the ham and its 60 second timer blip out of existence.

Stooping to scoop up the rest of my jewels, an electric chill runs up my spine. The rain falls silent. The world blurs and text in white spectral font begins scrolling across my entire field of view: Congratulations Xenia... Your unique capacity... To thrive… Has landed you a place… On New Earth… You have 24 hours… To find a companion … This game is ending But your *real* life is about to begin.
The message disappears and as the world un-blurs, a green 24 hour countdown clock begins ticking down.
Fayezilla, hovering directly in front of my face, waves her arms frantically.
“Xenia!” She squeals, snapping her tiny finger in my face as I blink back into awareness.
“Whoa!” Adrenaline rushes through me.
“What happened?” Fayezilla’s eyes are wide with concern.
“You didn’t get a message?” I fix my gaze on the fairy. “About the game ending?”
“Game ending?” Fayezilla cocks her head. “What does that even mean?”
“Let’s find that Kangaroo.” My pulse surges as I’m flooded with a hopeful excitement that I haven’t felt in decades. “I need to see Jenna.”
***Two Hours Later***

Rain pelts us as we approach the muddy bluegrass meadow where Mystic Depths’ recently killed NPCs respawn. The crack-of-a-whip sound of re-enlivening NPCs snaps through the air like a lasso show and my skin crackles with rolling glitches.

Some of the burlap-clad respawns wander towards waiting friends and family. Others trollop over to the market stalls where feral rats dart between crowded rows of vendors selling everything from broken weapons to healing crystals and of course fairy dust, ale and whatever else scratches your itch.

A humanoid Bloodhound in a rumpled beige trench coat, collar popped to his floppy ears, catches my eye from behind a redwood stump full of fairy dust paraphernalia. Taking a deep sniff in my direction he eyes me knowingly.

"Hey kid," his gravely voice beckons to me as he reaches a paw inside his detective-style coat, pulling out a dingy plastic Dustbuster. I squint at the device. The word Blaster has been sharpied over the word “Buster” and a plastic tube has been duct taped to the side.
"Wanna take a bite out of reality?" He winks, flicking the on switch.
The modified exhaust line lets out a high-pitched whine accompanied by a muffled barrage of slurs and insults from inside the plastic housing.
“Quiet down in there!” the bloodhound grumbles, shaking the device violently as it sprays a glittering cloud of green dust into the damp air between us.
Between my shoulder blades, I feel Fayezilla shake with rages as she buckles herself into her combat harness inside the metal case where she hides under my robes.

I Ignore them both, continuing to weave through the throngs of potato-sack-wearing shoppers until we reach a sagging boxing ring with a faded red banner across its base: “Out Box Treasure the Kangaroo and Win a Box of Treasure.”

paragraphs.text: POV Jenna -
2 - Swept Up
Neighborhoods - Inside Hyperspear (Inside SS Hyperspear Outside The Hyades Cluster)
“Paisley,” I sigh, “I don’t understand why you can’t just drive GG Myka’s truck to the re-spawn point.”
I gently rest my fifty-year-old woman hand on the pink, bedazzled Mac10 my great-granddaughter is pulling from the macrame side holster I made her. “It’s only twenty miles away.”

Her leather jacket groans as she steps back, gently tugging the gun from my grip. “You’re so old fashioned GG-Jenna,” Paisley giggles, swinging the Mac10 towards me. “Why don’t you come with?” She tongues her lip ring, rocking back on the heel of her hightop sneaker.
“Let’s ditch your old-timey supper club and hit up a *dance* club instead.” She shimmies towards me.
Chuckling, I shake my head, salt and pepper locks spilling across my face. “I want to see how far I can go this time.” I tuck a graying tendril behind my ear. “Before I naturally re-spawn.”
“Sounds like a drag.” Paisley raises her gun to her temple then pauses “Need anything from the market?”
“Well…” I click my tongue. “I am low on sugar.”
“I gotchu.” She pulls the trigger.
I turn away, my ears ringing as my sweet great-grandaughter’s beautiful face explodes into a thick red mist that splatters across the floor.

I shake my head at the bloody bits of skull on our white living room rug, fighting my impulse to grab my mop. I know by now that the stains will pixelate away before they set on the fabric, but the sight still stays with me longer than I’d like.
“Was that Paisley heading out?” Myka brushes his sandy gray locks away from his face as he trudges in from his den, “I wish she’d put a silencer on that thing.”
His green trousers swish as he strides over, planting a soft kiss on my lips.

“She’ll be back with some sugar in a bit.” I wrap my arms around Myka’s neck. “You’ve got the sweetest sugar in town though.” I focus on my husband's sparkling green eyes as Paisley’s abandoned body and associated gore pixelate out of existence.
Untangling myself from Myka, I turn towards the pile of laundry behind me. Laying one of Myka’s beige work shirts across the ironing board, I let out a lavender hiss of steam from the iron.

Just as I press the iron to his shirt, a sudden, rapid-fire clucking sound comes through the baby monitor on the coffee table. I’d originally set up the monitor so I could listen to the pleasant chatter of our front yard chickens while doing house work, but their natural predatory alarm behavior is an added bonus.
“Are you expecting anyone?” Myka eyes me curiously as he tip toes towards the front curtain. Before he can reach it, I hear our dog, Pajama’s bark-translating collar enthuse: “Xenia! Xenia is Coming”
“You’re confused old man?” Myka scratches our 200 year old mutt between his perpetually 5-year old ears. “Xenia lives a world away now.”
“Xenia!” Pajama bounces on his front paws “Xenia — Out Front!”
“His collar is broken again. It’s probably Cheryl from next door wanting to borrow some sugar again.”
Myka pulls the lace curtains aside and his jaw drops. “I think the collar’s actually fine!”
Hustling to the front door, he unbolts our lock, removing the door bar, before stepping aside to reveal my oldest friend in the Hyperspear Universe, looking not a day over 25.
Xenia Chloros, tips her straw cowgirl hat towards me, unleashing a cascade of dark curls as she bows.
“Holy wow!” I set down my iron and rush across the room to the front door.
“Is it really you?” I giggle, throwing my arms around her.
“I’m as real as I can be,” Xenia coos, pinching her arm.
Outside, I hear a neighbor shout in the distance: “Don’t forget the milk,” as a gunshot rings though the culdesac.
“I guess you Neighborhoods folks figured that trick out too.” Xenia follows me inside. “Taking the ol’ susie express to the market.” She winks at me.

“Well, I can’t say I love the idea of treating a gun like a taxi service,” I guide our guest into the kitchen, gesturing for her to take a seat at the table Myka had carved for my hundredth birthday. “But, there’s just so many people and so much traffic everywhere. Our neighbor Cheryl has over a thousand grand kids at this point.” I shrug. “It gets exhausting.”

“Tell me about it.” Xenia rolls her eyes as she slides into a wickerback chair that Myka made last winter. “It’s all I can do to get a fresh kill home without having three mobs of Orcs try to rob me before I reach the entrance to my lair.”
“Speaking of.” I ease myself into a creaky wicker chair across from Xenia. “What brings you by my neck of the woods?”
“Son of a glitch!” Xenia squeezes her eyes shut.
“I’d really hoped you got the same system message I did.” Her eyes bore pleadingly into mine, prompting me to pick up on some subliminal cue.
Pursing my lips I shake my head. “Sorry.” I shrug. “I have no idea what you’re talking about.”
My heart sinks as Xenia relays the cryptic message she’d received eleven hours earlier.
“Have you slept?” Myka slinks over setting a cup of tea in front of Xenia as he slides into a chair beside me.
Leaning towards him, Xenia rests her elbows on the table. “I’ve got enlivening magic that replaces the need to slee- slee- s- ss–”
My friend's entire torso pixelates, static popping violently in the air around her.
“Whoa.” Myka and I throw our chairs back, leaping away from the sparks.
Pajama, who had been sleeping by Myka’s feet, springs up, hackles raised as he growls accusingly at Xenia.
“I’ve never seen a glitch that intense before.” I spring towards Myka, burrowing my face into his starchy ranger shirt. A pop of electricity surges through me as my fingers pixelate.
Myka frowns at me, before peering down at his own pixelating fingers.
Suddenly, the popping stops and as we all de-pixelate, Xenia’s whole frame slumps.
“I have more details.” She whispers, gesturing for us to sit down.
Sucking my sore fingers, I slide into a seat across from Xenia. Myka takes a step back, crossing his arms as he leans against the wall as Pajama lays down by his feet.
Lowering her eyes, Xenia clears her throat. “So I guess, Hyperspear, ” taps her fingers on the table “Wants to just totally focus on this New Earth thing.”
I gulp down air.
“So,” she stammers, “it’s going to archive all the other game worlds and assets–including NPCs.”
I gasp.
Myka steps away from the wall, casting a heavy stare at Xenia. “And then we’re all dead?”
“Why are you looking at *me* like that?” Xenia jumps up from her chair, glaring at Myka. “As far as I know, I don’t have a choice about any of this.”
“So why are you here then?” Myka blurts coldly.
“Don’t fight.” I rise to my feet, my eyeballs dancing between my husband and the best friend I’ve ever had.

“Sorry.” Xenia ducks her head. “I know this is upsetting news.” She lifts her eyes to mine. “I think whoever’s left behind–” She pauses, clearly trying to spin up some cotton candy fantasy for me to eat up. “They probably just feel like they’re in a nice happy sleep.”
“Yeah I’ll bet.” Myka scoffs.
Xenia’s lips twitch into a weak smile. “If Hyperspear wanted to hard delete us, it would have by now.”
Myka lets out a defeated sigh as he leans back against the wall.
“Maybe if—” Xenia takes a deep breath. “—When—” She nods at Myka. “When things are going well on New Earth,” she casts her smile my way, “I’m sure we can find a way to bring your whole family there.”
A high-pitched shriek of chicken clucks blares through the flock monitor in the living room.
Xenia goes rigid. Cocking her ear towards the ceiling, her face drops. “A pair of helicopters is approaching from the west.” Her eyeballs turn to ellipses as she accesses her game menu.
Xenia’s pupils return and she locks eyes with me: “They’re less than a mile away.”
“Helicopters are taking us to New Earth?” I squint at Xenia, confused, as the distant oscillating pulse of chopper blades grows louder.
“No. I have no idea why the helicopters are coming.” She shrugs. “I’m here because I get to bring a companion with me to New Earth.”
The front windows rattle as the first helicopter nears.
“And,” Xenia shouts above the roar of the blades, “I choose you, Jenna Boo.” She clasps my shoulder warmly.
My heart drops.
“What?” I struggle to breath as the idea of existing in a world without Myka smashes into my chest like a sledge hammer.
“Come to New Earth with me!” Xenia bellows, dropping to her knee as she reaches for my hand.
“No!” I slap her hand away, glaring. “How are you being so flippant about this.”
Something buzzes between Xenia’s shoulders as a shrill voice squeals. “You could take me and you want to take her?”
The helicopter is now directly above our house.
“Great.” Xenia squeezes her septum. “This is going really well.”
My eyes drift to the ceiling as something thuds onto our roof, sending Pajama into a barking fit.
“Duck and Cover! Duck and Cover!” PJ’s collar blares as I hear the unfortunately familiar sound of a helicopter spinning out of control.

Zooming into the front room, Pajama wriggles under the couch as the rest of us dive under the kitchen table, heads ducked, hands clasped over our ears and necks as the helicopter careens into a neighbor’s roof, releasing a hot percussive blast of energy that shatters every window in the house, shaking plaster loose from the ceilings.
“GG Myka!” Squinting through the, now tattered, front curtains I catch a glimpse of Paisley precariously clinging to the rain gutters as she dangles above the front porch.
“Paisley’s home! Paisley! Home!” Pajama’s collar enthuses as he wriggles out from under the couch, his tail swishing wildly as he prances in circles in front of the window.
Coughing, I scramble out from under the table.
Beside me, Xenia extends her arm towards my great-granddaughter, shouting. “Lasso Target”.
Nothing happens.
“Magic doesn’t work here, Chosen One.” Myka shoulder-checks Xenia as he hustles into the front room and out the window.
“Right,” Xenia lets her arm fall lamely to her side. “I guess I need to get used to doing things the old fashioned way.”
Myka, clutching paisley in his arms, steps back through the front window as the second chopper descends.
He sets Paisley on her feet and she rushes over to me, Pajama trailing behind.
“A riot broke out at the market.” She shouts over the din of the landing chopper.
“They’re saying we only have like twelve hours.” She blinks away a tear “Until Hyperspear shuts down its game worlds.”
“Did you really have to steal another helicopter though, dear?” I shout, wrapping my arms around my quirky, smart, kind, GGD.
“Didn’t you hear me?” Paisley’s chest heaves as she pulls away from my embrace. “We have twelve hours left to live and you seriously care about some stolen chopper?”
Air wooshes through the house as the second helicopter touches down in the cul de sac.
A tall man and his hulking dog hop out, striding casually toward the front porch while Pajama launches into another barking fit, his collar spewing expletives at the strangers.
“You can’t just go stealing folks' helicopters every time someone cries doomsday.” A man’s cold booming voice chastises.
“Well what do ya know!” The stranger laughs as his dog goes rigid, pinning its front leg to its torso.
“Arrow here thinks you have a fairy in there.” He tussles the dog's ears.
“Your dog’s mistaken.” Myka steps in front of Paisley and me, grabbing Pajama’s collar as the man raises his AR, perforating the wall of the front room with bullets.

From the corner of my eye I see something on Xenia's back quiver as she grabs the meat cleaver from my butcher block and charges into the front room, where the black-clad stranger is now easing his leg through the front window.
“Wait!” A shrill voice between Xenia’s shoulders shrieks. “I’m not in my battle harness ye—”
Xenia launches herself at the man and with swift hacking chops cleaves his leg off at the hip.
The man’s leg drops to the floor, spinning like a pinwheel as cartoonish blood gushes in all directions.
“I’ve been there for you for decades” A voice from Xenia’s back complains as she skillfully dismembers the fairy poacher. “And you want to take this normie?”
I turn away, stomach lurching, as she turns towards the man’s dog.
“Not the dog Xenia.” I fight back tears, stroking Pajama’s ears as Myka envelops me in a comforting embrace.
“All good now!” Xenia boasts, glass crunching underfoot as she hoists herself back in through the broken window, her pet fairy or whatever continuing to heckle her.
“Hellloo Pretty Stranger!” Paisley coos, ignoring the derision spewing from Xenia’s posterior, as she sidles over to my friend.
“Thank you so much for handling that bad guy.” Paisley grabs Xenia’s hand forcing her into an enthusiastic handshake. “I’m Paisley.”
I stare incredulously at my pandering progeny while I try to think of the most convincing way to tell my dearest friend that she needs to run away to the New World with my husband.
“You don't wanna take me.” I stammer.
Xenia’s back rumbles violently and a red-pulsating fairy bursts out from her shirt collar soaring into the air above Xenia’s head.

“See you stupid glitch. She doesn’t even want to go” The chirpy voiced fairy sasses out her hip, pointing an accusing finger at Xenia. “What better companion could you possibly want than the most sought after being in all of Hyperspear.” The fairy pouts, sending a cloud of sparkling dust into the air around her. ”What can this old hag over here,” the rude pixie eyes me disdainfully, “possibly have to offer that I don’t?”
“Take Myka!” I blurt.

Xenia shakes her head. “It has to be you, Jenna.” Setting the blood-speckled meat cleaver on the kitchen counter, Xenia steps towards me. “The message said I was chosen because of my ability to thrive.” She rests her bloody hand on my shoulder. “You’re the one who taught me how to thrive.”
We pitch our cases to Xenia for hours, me pleading with her to take Myka who I know will be the most useful. Myka trying to convince me to shut up and Paisley and Fayezilla advocating for themselves.
Xenia hasn’t budged on her decision when red sixty second count down clocks appear above Myka, Paisley and Fayezilla’s heads.
Xenia has a clock too, but hers is green. Glancing up, I see that mine’s green too.
Sobbing, I throw myself into Myka’s arms and squeeze my eyes shut while Pajama nuzzles his face between Myka and me.
“Jenna leaks sad water.” Pajama’s collar laments.
“Hold me when you go.” Paisley pleads to Xenia. “Maybe you can bring me with you too.” She wraps herself around Xenia’s arm.
Gunshots and explosions ring through the streets outside.
I bury my face deeper into my husband’s shoulder, hoping maybe I’ll suffocate and respawn and I won’t have to wake up in some new world where he no longer exists.
Opening my eyes, I take a last look at the world I’ve inhabited for two centuries.
Xenia is cradling Paisley under one arm.
Four seconds.
Fayezilla is slowly backing away from Xenia’s face.
Three seconds.
Fayezilla lays flat in the air, her fist extended in front of her face.
Two seconds.
A sonic burst booms from the spot where Fayezilla had been.
One second.
Xenia’s head jolts back, the pink fairy’s heels protruding from her mouth.

paragraphs.text: POV DIEGO
3 - DAY 1
NEW EARTH - THE HOPEFUL MOUNTAIN TOP
Bright White… Searing Pixelations of Pain… My heartbeat thumps in my chest, blood rushes through dry veins, igniting my bare nerves in fiery pain as they sizzle to life.

A cacophony of anguished screams and groans erupt around me and I hear myself join in, as skull-splitting pain flares through my brain. My head throbs as two hundred years of archived memories are seared into my supple brain tissue.

Helpless and naked, I collapse into a ball on the jagged, hard surface beneath me, pinning my palms against my ears. For countless agonizing minutes, I jerk and writhe on a floor that seems to be made of shattered glass and hair. And then suddenly it stops.

My headache subsides and the vibrance of New Earth’s sounds and smells overwhelms my senses. The acrid stench of sulfur and ash sting my nostrils as layers of sound bombard my ears – people moaning, the sharp, squawking caws of distant birds, a low pulsating rumble that hums across the shattered surface below me. I tip my head back and blink my eyes open, admiring the vast cerulean sky —until I turn my gaze towards the warm light of the single star above. The light pierces my eyeballs.

Dang it! I throw my bloody scratched arm across my face, shielding my fragile retinas from the blazing sunlight. Bright spots continue to dance across my vision even with my eyelids snapped shut and I chastise myself for not remembering that corporeal beings can be blinded just by looking at their star.

My tongue feels like a dry thumb as I lick my cracked, calloused lips and cautiously blink my eyes open again. As the world comes into focus, I realize I’m at the bottom of some sort of volcanic crater: about thirty feet deep and fifty feet across. Surrounding me are several dozen naked, fit, extremely long-haired, young adult humans.

Pressing into the shards of rock on the crater floor, I attempt to stand, but my toes tangle in some coarse fiber, and I yelp in surprise as I crash down hard, grinding my hands and knees into the sharp floor.

“Gwwahh!” I hear a slightly off version of my voice bellow as my toes rip out strands of the impressively long, thick, beard sprouting from my chin sending pinpricks of pain radiating through my entire face. Twiddling my toes, I untangle my beard, catching sight of the five foot long mane of hair draping over my beef-cake shoulders. A young man's laugh rumbles out of me.
Sweet! I’m like Mr. Universe.
“Daaah–Dahad” a young man calls out beside me and I suddenly remember my traveling companion.

“Lu– lulu,” my dry, virgin mouth struggles to form my son's name. “Luuuu.” I wave both hands over my head as a yeti-bearded, twenty-five-year-old version of my two-hundred-year-old boy toddles towards me, six feet of dark locks trailing behind him.
“Luke,” my voice is strong and clear now.
Youthful jubilance gushes through me as I awkwardly tackle Luke, pulling him into a loose side embrace.
“Dad!” Luke bellows, exuberantly, flexing his forearms. “Look how freakin’ swole we are!”
“And these ladies” He nudges me with his elbow, gesturing around the crater where the other Hopefuls are now sharing their first moments on New Earth with their own —hairy, naked-– companions.

“Look at that!” I marvel, stooping to the crater floor, picking up a two-foot-long, black wing feather that looks like it’s from a massive chicken. “Do you think this world has giant chickens?” I twirl the feather between my fingers as my mind flicks back two hundred years to my first, narrowly won battle as an NPC — against a giant black rooster.
Re-focusing on the present moment, I turn to Luke. “I can’t wait to get out of this hole and see what other kinds of flora and fauna might be here!”
“Aww, Dad,” Luke snickers, “you couldn’t even make it five minutes on New Earth without thinking about gardening.”
“Yeah well,” I guffaw, “I guess that’s why Hyperspear asked me to come here and why you’re just a plus one.” I clap Luke on the back, playfully.
“Are you kidding me?!” An outraged voice jars me from the father-son moment.
A few yards away, a completely hairless man pumps his fist at the sky as he screams: “You made me bald here too?!”
On the other side of the crowd a woman’s voice wails: “My Wings? Where are my wings?”
“I can’t use magic!” A deep-voiced man grumbles.
Complaints swirl all around : “I can’t access a game menu!”, “Why are we all humans?”, “My hunger level is 10!”

A short blond lady sidles over to me, tipping her head toward the bald man, whose sweating head is glistening in the mid-day sun. “The Gleam over there’s lucky,” She chuckles. “It’ll take me an hour just to braid this mane I’ve got.”
The Gleam casts a biting look our way before stomping indignantly off towards the shaded crater wall.
“I like the way your head gleams, babe”, a red-haired lady coos, hurrying after him.
“Jenna!” A voice calls out from the middle of the crowd, making my ears perk as ancient memories of old friends begin to surface.
“Jen–na why aren’t you answering me?” The familiar voice calls.
“Xenia?” The name comes out of my mouth before I even remember who she is.

Squinting in the direction of the dark-maned damsel sidling through the crowd, an epiphany goes off in my brain. Two centuries ago, before The Great Provincial Placement locked us into different game worlds, Xenia and Jenna had been two of my closest friends.
My heart flutters as warm, ancient memories of shared meals and hard won battles resurface.
“Diego?” The two girls chime in unison.

Beside me, Luke turns to face my approaching friends. “Are these the girls that…” His voice trails off as his gaze settles on Xenia’s chest. “... the girls that helped save me when that Darcy lady kidnapped me?”
Stopping a couple feet away, Jenna shyly arranges her hair to cover her lady parts, offering Luke and me a weak smile and an unenthusiastic wave.
I tuck my own long locks between my legs as Xenia trudges over to Luke.
“Can this be baby Luke?” She narrows her eyes at my son. “ –oggling my boo–.”
Xenia’s voice suddenly sputters, her left eye twitching wildly as her shoulders go rigid.
Luke steps back, shooting Jenna and me a concerned look.
Squeezing her eyes shut, Xenia crosses her arms over her chest stammering: “I think some part of my brain is still bootloading.”
“I haven’t felt any glitches yet.” Jenna mumbles. “I thought we were supposed to be leaving those behind.”
The sunlight dims and l squint up at the clouds beginning to form in the sky above our crater.
“Your glitchiness may be the least of your worries.” I frown. “If it starts storming, this crater’s going to fill up like a bucket.
Jamming my index finger and thumb in my mouth I let out a piercing whistle. The sound reverberates around the crater silencing the grumbling hopefuls.

“Hey folks, let’s not forge—” I clear my throat. “—We’re not only lucky to be here, but we also don’t have a choice.” I flash an exaggerated smile and point at the sky. “And we’re probably being watched.”
My lacerated feet sting with each step as I crunch across the crater floor, pacing amongst my fellow Hopefuls. “We need to work together and try to stay positive.”

The crowd makes room for me as I stride towards the bald man who's making a bloody mess of his hands attempting to get purchase on a horizontal crack in the rock wall while his companion gnaws at a strand of her hair. “I want to make him gloves.” She pauses, staring up at me helplessly.

Stooping, I dig through the chunks of jagged rocks by my feet until I find a cracked, jagged chunk of fossilized lighting, fulgurite. Using the jagged edge, I saw off a thick, five-foot long lock of my own hair and hand it to the woman.
Turning back to the crowd I cup my hands around my mouth. “Folks, our fellow Hopefuls over here have the right idea—” I tip my face up towards the clouds. “—we need to get out of this dang hole!”

Jenna, careful to keep the bulk of hair tucked between her legs, pulls out a strand of her chestnut locks and slinks towards me. “Maybe we can make ropes from our hair and then if someone here’s really good at climbing they can get up there and we can pull ourselves out. “Take my hair,” she offers, smiling shyly.
Everyone murmurs in approval.

“Whoa, Dudes, Check this Out!” A green-eyed adonis shouts from the back of the crowd, there’s a lava tube or something over here. I think I felt a draft. Maybe we can get out of this dungeon pit if we go this way.”

My stomach clenches at the mention of a dungeon. I spent two hundred years tending digital crops inside a cozy farming sim—a game originally designed for toddlers and bored housewives. I’d been eager for some real adventure, but my last experience in a dungeon world left deep scars. My heart races as I realize there could be horrors beyond my imagination waiting outside this crater. And the pain out there will be real. And death… death will be forever.

I take a long steadying breath before hollering to the crowd: “Folks, I think maybe we should divide into two teams and look into the tunnel as well as getting some rope together for climbing up and out.”

Finn, who discovered the lava tubes earlier, sets off with Luke and Xenia to explore the cave while the rest of us break into small groups, severing and twisting our locks into strands of twine while chatting and getting to know one another.
While we work, cumulonimbus clouds form ominously overhead, chilling the warm humid air.

Jenna, sitting across from me, furrows her brow. “Its been at least half an hour since Xenia and Luke went down in that cave.” Setting down her hairtwine, she hugs her shoulders “If it starts rainining, will the cave fill with water?”
Thunder rumbles in the distance as a frigid raindrop splatters on my bare shoulder, sending a chill ripping through my youthful, muscular frame.
“Go holler down there. I bet your voice will echo down to them,” I urge Jenna as I hop to my feet.
“Hey folks!” I shout across the crater. “I think we have enough rope. Lets start building a human pyramid or whatever we need to do to start getting to higher ground!”
“I was a parkourist chimpanzee in a skate park gameworld.” Cade, A lanky, sandy haired man hops to his feet. “Give me the rope and I should be able to scale my way up there.”
The Gleam hurries over and hands a long rope of braided hairtwine to Cade. “Get up there then!”

Wrapping the braided rope across his chest, Cade springs towards the wall, easily catching a jagged handhold with his right hand. Blood drips from his fingers as he scrambles for purchase with his feet. Once he has a toehold, he deftly scrambles up the wall, hoisting himself from one jagged hold to the next until his fingers grip the precipice.

Cheers echo off the crater walls as Cade rolls over onto his back beside the lip of the crater. Flexing his bleeding fingers, Cade stands and surveys the world beyond the crater. “This is like nothing I’ve ever seen,” he marvels, lowering himself to his stomach before casting an end of the hair rope down into the crater.
The crowd is making their way towards the rope, when Finn wriggles up from the lava tube, followed by Xenia and finally Luke.
“We found a way into a forest.” Luke exclaims.
“There are definitely some biiiig monsters out there though.” Xenia sighs.
Suddenly, the sky opens up. Water rushes down the crater walls creating a current that flows down the lava tube.

Locking arms with Jenna, I charge towards Cade’s outstretched braid of hair. “Get up there girl!” I shout to her before turning towards the panicked throng of Hopefuls who are also rushing towards the rope.
“Everyone lock arms and get to the wall. Don’t let the water flush you down the lava tube!” I beckon. “One at a time up the rope.”

The water in the bottom of the crater is ankle deep by the time Jenna reaches the top, and lowers a second hair rope down. Bracing myself against the frigid, rushing deluge, I direct traffic, handing ropes off to The Gleam and his companion up next. The pair easily rocket up the braids of hair like trained soldiers before lowering two more ropes down. One after another the Hopefuls climb out of the crater, helping the stragglers up after them, until I’m the last one, standing thigh deep in the surging water.
Flinging myself at the wall, I jump up and grab hold of the nearest hair rope. Hand over hand I pull myself up, flopping onto my side, my chest heaving as I reach the top.

Staring out between flashes of lightning, I take in the view. We’re on a granite plateau about the size of a baseball diamond, two stories above the canopy of a subtropical forest, brimming with towering conifers and deciduous trees clustered around dark swamps with a massive, swollen river winding through the expanse.
A few yards away, The Gleam is helping his companion steady herself as she crouches with her heels touching. “We need to spread out so we don't draw an arc,” he shouts.
“Stand like my wife Dora.” The Gleam nods to his companion as he strides towards Jenna. “Keep your heels together.” He nods at her toes.
The rain begins to subside, but the wind seems to be picking up as I space myself out from my fellows on the plateau.

I’m struggling to click my heels together when a sound like a tearing canvas rips through the air, followed by a singular, deafening CRACK. A shockwave sends a massive puff of pulverized granite dust rolling across the plateau. Then the air grows still.
Around me, the Hopefuls begin helping each other up, surveying the fallout on the plateau.
“I think there’s writing down there.” Jenna points down into the crater.
I creep over beside her, I watch as the rainwater drains down the lava tube revealing a message etched on the crater floor as if by a laser:
By the dawn of Day 3, you must designate a singular Voice. That Voice will speak a manifest of up to 100 physical assets from the Hyperspear archives.
COMPLIANCE MATRIX:
Quantity: One individual unit per asset slot. Grouped containers (boxes of…, barrels of…, bundles of…) will fail to materialize.
Scale: No asset may exceed the volume of a standard shipping container.
Status: Inanimate objects only. Sentient, biological, or computational entities are barred.
Environment: New Earth operates on absolute physics. Assets reliant on magic, fantasy mechanics, or self-materialization will be rendered permanently inert.
Form: Solids only; liquids and gases will fail to materialize.
Choose wisely.

paragraphs.text: POV DIEGO
5 - DINO NUGGETS
NEW EARTH - HOPEFUL MOUNTAINTOP
“Nice work Alana,” I turn away from the “The Medical, Chemical, & Dietary Committee”, striding towards a tall blonde with a shaggy A-frame haircut who’s waiving me down.

“Why is he,” Sage huffs, side-eyeing Finn, “in the Textiles, and Domestic Committee?” She hitches up her macrame bikini top—a flawless piece of tailoring she’d spent hours weaving from her own blond locks.
A few yards away, Finn, a green-eyed adonis is lying fully nude atop a tangled pile of his own hair twine. A curtain of jaw length dreadlocks brush the granite cliff top as he admires his own shadow.
“He was a talking fish in Hyperspear,” Sage gripes. “He doesn’t even know what a textile is and he’s never had a home!”

I pull up my hair-woven loincloth as my empty stomach grumbles. Finn had asked to lead an exploratory team out the volcano tubes, but after the first storm, the tubes were so clogged with rocks and debris they were impassable.
“Look Sage,” I sigh, “We’re all hungry and depleted, but we’re on a tight deadline and he’s very knowledgeable about nets and plumbing.”
“I had the best idea Mr. Diego!” Finn beams, trotting over to me. “My item is going to be a tank for water the size of a shipping container.”
“Nice,” I nod in approval.
Placing two fingers in my mouth, I let out a piercing whistle. Around me, the clusters of Hopefuls pause their committee discussions and turn.
“Finn is making his item the exact size of a shipping container.” I clap Finn on the back pridefully. “Maybe we should all think about doing th–”
A deafening guttural shriek, louder than anything I’ve ever heard, echoes up from the forest floor, cutting me off.

Concerned muttering erupts. The groups of asset committees instantly crowd together forming a single, cowering mass in the center of Hopeful Mountaintop while the intermittent shrieks continue to assault our ears.

Suddenly, the crowd parts. Xenia, who’s wound her hair-twine around herself like a black tube dress, forces her way to the edge of the cluster of Hopefuls and turns to face us. Her mouth moves like she’s shouting something, but the jungle noises swallow the sound of her voice.

I furrow my brow as she begins frustratedly wriggling her shoulders and hopping up and down,her left eye blinking furiously. Wrestling herself to stillness, she points at her chest, then flashes a two-finger ‘V’ from her eyes towards the cliff’s edge. I hustle towards her, falling in step beside her.
We charge across the granite expanse, stopping a yard from the drop-off. Xenia drops to her belly and I follow suit.

We army-crawl, side-by-side across the hot stone and peer over the precipice. Straight below us, a half-dozen four foot tall long-necked reptilian chickens with clawed hands at the end of their tiny wings, are scrambling up a fallen redwood trunk that’s propped against the wall of our plateau. Shaking their dorsal fin mohawks, as they approach the cliff wall, they stand upright.
Frantic flapping their wings, the chickens from hell somehow generate enough downward force to take several vertical steps up the sheer cliff.
Their toothless maws chomp at the air just a few yards below us before they slide, one-by-one back down into the canopy below.

Another pair of Dino Nuggets from hell, twice the size of the first six, charge up the tree trunk. Each of the heavier predators scruffs one of the juveniles by the back of the neck. Swinging them back like pendulums, they catapult the young ones straight at us.
The two smaller ones frantically flap their feeble wings uselessly as they collide with the granite cliff, clawing for purchase just below our faces before plunging back down into the trees.
Xenia and I exchange a horrified look as we both slither back away from the edge.
“They’re running up the cliff!” I holler, bolting to my feet and sprinting into the crowd.
“Some kind of Dino Nuggets from Hell are running up the dang cliff!”
“Look for anything you can use as a weapon!” Xenia barks, catching her breath beside me as she begins unwinding her hair dress.
Around us, everyone frantically drops to their hands and knees, searching for sharp rocks.
The first Dino Nugget lands atop the plateau with a resounding thud, letting out a piercing bass-heavy hiss. Feathers bristling, its toothless beak snaps in our direction.

The Hopefuls scream in shock and horror as a second creature catapults over the lip of the stone, immediately followed by one of the massive adults, who barely clearing the clifftop, rolls towards us.

Xenia reacts instantly. Her hands blur as she rips at the bottom of her frizzy tube top dress, unraveling a long, thick strand of the black hair-twine she’d spun. With her practiced muscle memory from Hyperspear, she loops the cord, knotting it into a makeshift lasso as she positions herself between the approaching beasts and the cowering Hopefuls.
As we back away from the trio of Dino Nuggets, Sage is left standing, frozen with fear, a few dozen yards ahead of the crowd of Hopefuls.
“Get back!” I scream to Sage, stepping forward to pull her back.
I’m a second too late. The adult theropod lunges across the granite with terrifying, mechanical speed. Its blunt, muscular head slams into Sage, knocking her flat onto the stone.
The juvenile creatures swarm. Sage shrieks—a raw, agonizing sound —as the monsters’ toothless maws clamp down and rip her limbs apart.

The actual real-world gore unraveling before me chills my blood. Doubling over, my stomach heaves. Water and bugs splatter ont the hot granite in front of me as the chaotic blur of thrashing, brightly colored feathers and tearing skin continues.

Around me, the Hopefuls erupt into panic, scattering, screaming in all directions. With a sickening crack, a blood-slicked, splintered femur slides across the smooth stone, spinning to a halt at Xenia’s feet.

She doesn't hesitate. Dropping low, Xenia scoops up the jagged bone with one hand while swinging her hair lasso with the other. She whips the black cord through the air. The loop catches one of the smaller Dino Nuggets cleanly around its feathered neck.
With a guttural grunt, Xenia plants her bare feet, yanking the rope back with all her weight. The surprised creature topples off balance, squawking as it slides across the granite toward her.

When it stumbles into range, Xenia drives the splintered end of Sage’s femur straight up into the creature's massive, black eye socket. The beast screeches, a high-pitched trill of agony. Before it can shake her off, Xenia releases the rope, launching herself forward. Tucking her chin, she braces her arm like a helmet, headbutting the creature towards the edge of the cliff.
The dazed dinosaur stumbles backward, losing its footing on the round edge of the precipice, and plunges out of sight, shrieking as it falls through the forest canopy below.
The remaining predators freeze, turning their blood-stained beaks toward Xenia, preparing to charge.
Suddenly, the air pressure drops. It’s so fast my ears pop. Then, a blinding flash and a deafening, metallic crack shatter the sky.

A massive bolt of purple-white lightning strikes from the cloudless sky above, slamming directly into the large Dino Nugget. The quartz in the granite floor liquifies around the creature forming a crater around it.

CRACK! another bolt arcs down, precisely pinpointing the remaining juvenile, forming a second puddle of lightning glass. The sound of the strike is still ringing in my ears as five more bolts strike the forest in quick succession. The ground vibrates violently beneath my feet as a halo of blistering heat grows around the Dino Nuggets’ carcasses.
And then the deafening silence of the mountaintop returns, broken only by the whimpering of the stunned Hopefuls and the crackling hissing Dino Nuggets.

The smell of barbecued meat fills the crisp air, making my empty stomach grumble. A couple dozen hopefuls surge towards the smoking carcasses, screaming in pain as the crackling glass cuts and burns their soft feet.

“Hey dumb dumbs,” Xenia chides, her naked form striding towards the crowd around the larger Dino Nugget. “You shouldn’t even think about touching Lightning meat for at least an hour after the strike.”

A few paces away, Jenna in a hairy tube dress that matches her friend’s, sits on the hot stone floor clutching her knees. Her bare shoulders tremble as her wide eyes dart between the steaming dino carcasses and Sage’s bloody remains, strewn across the plateau.
Luke, in hair twine board shorts, sidles over to Jenna. Crouching he drapes his arm around her.
Turning away from the sizzling Dino Nugget, Xenia catches Jenna’s eye.
The cowering girl suddenly straightens up, climbing to her feet before striding to a lonely patch of granite away from the throngs of terrorized hopefuls.
“Hyperspear saved us!” Finn gleefully screams as he wanders up from behind.
“Saved us?!” The Gleam scoffs, emerging from the crowd around the larger Dino Nugget.

“Did you not see Sage just get ripped apart?” The bald man sneers, shoulder checking Finn as he walks past. “Were you not just torn from your happy home in Hyperspear and slapped down on some barren rock.” The Gleam hikes up the hair skirt we made for him, glaring accusingly at me.
“You idiots need to stop playing Hyperspear’s twisted game.” The sun gleams off his bald sweaty head momentarily blinding me as several Hopefuls wander over, grumbling in agreement.
“So what are you going to do?” I step towards The Gleam. “Walk away from the gifts it wants to give us.” I eye him incredulously. “You want to go fight the monsters in the jungle on your own?”
“Exactly.” He scoffs. “Those items will be cursed.” He shakes his head. “This whole New Earth thing is just some cruel new game for us to play.”
Ten or eleven Hopefuls are now clustered around The Gleam nodding in agreement.
“There were more of these little dino-birds down there, huh?” The Gleam turns towards Xenia. “Those other lightning bolts took out the rest of the flock right?”
“I think so, yes.” Xenia confirms. “There were at least four others down there.”

“Anyone who thinks two hundred years was long enough to be ground down under Hyperspear’s all powerful thumb.” The Gleam beckons. “Come with me.” He strides towards the massive ball of hair-rope that everyone (except him) had been weaving, to lower ourselves down from the plateau.
“Come on Xenia.” The gleam extends his hand towards my friend. “Come be the beautiful warrior princess I know you are.”
Xenia’s left eye twitches wildly as she shakes her head stepping behind me.

“What about you, Luke?” The Gleam flashes a covetous smile at my son, gesturing toward the rope. “Aren’t you ready to cut the cord and find out what life is like without your overbearing father breathing down your neck.”
Luke strides over standing beside Xenia, behind me.

“We know we can kill these creatures with the right tools.” The Gleam crosses the plateau, approaching Jenna. “If you were plunked down here against my will.” He rests a sympathetic hand on Jenna’s frail shoulder. “I can certainly relate.” Pivoting on his heel he marches back to the rope. “If you’ve had enough of being Hyperspear’s hapless puppet.” He snatches up the coil, slipping it over his shoulder. “Follow me.” The Gleam marches to the shallow cave, carefully knotting the end of the rope around a stalagmite as he runs the length of it along a groove in the plateau’s floor.
